comparisons.peer_summary: The Federal Reserve and OCC establish capital and liquidity requirements consistent with Basel III, with ongoing global refinements and U.S. proposals to revise risk-based capital requirements for large banks; finalization and implementation dates for U.S. rules remain uncertain, while EU and UK rules have been finalized with phased implementation through 2027 and transitional arrangements until 2030-2032.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs disclose the impact of EU Basel III Revisions on cross-border banking services. JPMorgan notes that EU regulators have finalized Basel III rules effective January 1, 2025, with a delayed market risk aspect. Similarly, Goldman Sachs states that the EU introduced restrictions on cross-border provision of core banking services (deposit-taking, lending, commitments) as part of Basel III, requiring new contracts to be executed out of EU subsidiaries like GSBE, with a grandfathering provision for pre-June 2026 contracts.

sentences.text: As part of its implementation of the Basel III Revisions, the E.U. introduced new restrictions on the provision of certain "core" banking services (i.e., deposit-taking, lending and the provision of commitments and guarantees) cross-border into the E.U. Contracts in place before June 2026 will be subject to a "grandfathering" provision and new core banking services will need to be executed out of our subsidiaries established in the E.U., including GSBE.
In the EU and U.K., regulators have finalized the rules implementing their Basel III frameworks.
The new rules became effective in the EU beginning January 1, 2025, with market risk aspects delayed until January 1, 2026.
